did_you_know.text: Did you know? Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, from the tribe of Issachar, judged Israel after Abimelech and lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
Did you know? Tola judged Israel for twenty-three years, and after he died, he was buried in Shamir.
Did you know? Jair the Gileadite rose up after Tola and judged Israel for twenty-two years.
Did you know? Jair had thirty sons, each of whom rode a donkey, and his sons owned thirty towns called Havvoth-jair in the land of Gilead.
Did you know? The Israelites served not only the Baals and the Ashtoreths, but also the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites, and the Philistines.
Did you know? For eighteen years, the Ammonites oppressed the Israelites who lived east of the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.
Did you know? Then the Ammonites crossed the Jordan and also fought against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in great distress.
Did you know? The Israelites confessed their sin, saying, “We have sinned against you,” and connected their distress with abandoning the LORD and serving the Baals.
Did you know? In his reply, the LORD reminded the Israelites of earlier deliverances from Egypt, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines, as well as from Sidon, Amalek, and the Meunites.
Did you know? After the Israelites removed the foreign gods from among them and returned to serving the LORD, it is said, “He could no longer bear Israel’s misery.”

Did you know? When the Ammonites camped in Gilead and the Israelites gathered at Mizpah, the leaders of Gilead asked for a leader who would begin fighting the Ammonites and become the head of all who lived in Gilead.
